items.title: The endless invasions: Spatiotemporal patterns of non-native insects in China
items.abstract: NeoBiota 109: 203-215 DOI: 10.3897/neobiota.109.184222 Authors: Shuo Peng, Yibo Zhang, Cang Hui, Khalid Haddi, Yujia Qin, Zhihong Li, Zihua Zhao Abstract: Biological invasions have been defined as one striking indicator of the Anthropocene epoch, with more species being translocated beyond their native range by human activities. The inventory of non-native species in a region provides basic information for further exploration of biological invasions. We compiled a checklist of non-native insects in China and then analyzed their diversity at species level and invasion patterns. In total, 241 species of non-native insects were recorded in China, belonging to 8 orders and 181 genera. Coleoptera, Hemiptera, and Lepidoptera were the top three largest orders. Asia and North America donated most species of non-native insects, with Oceania contributing the fewest. The spatial distribution of non-native insects showed a decrease from coastal areas to inland regions, and inland border regions of Yunnan and Xinjiang had more first records of non-native species. Additionally, the number of non-native insect species has increased exponentially since 1900. Non-native insects were most likely introduced into China by stowaway and by contaminant, with a preference for terrestrial ecosystem. The overview of non-native insects in China provides a comprehensive perspective on their invasion patterns, helping to elucidate the dynamics of non-native insects and contributing to a balanced understanding of their global patterns.
